Full power!|Admiral Gorin orders his crew to try and avoid the oncoming Star Destroyer collision|audio=Gorin.flac|}} '''Gorin''' was a [[human]] who served as an [[admiral]] in the [[Imperial Navy|naval forces]] of the [[Galactic Empire]] during the [[Galactic Civil War]] against the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic]]. He [[Commanding officer|commanded]] the [[Imperial I-class Star Destroyer|''Imperial I''-class Star Destroyer]] ''[[Intimidator]]'' and served as [[Orbital Command]] for the [[Scarif fleet|Imperial forces]] stationed above the [[planet]] [[Scarif]], including the [[Shield Gate]] that allowed access to the world. In [[1 BBY]], the [[Rebel Alliance Navy|Alliance Fleet]] [[Battle of Scarif|attacked]] Gorin's forces in order to aid [[Rogue One|rebel forces]] that had already infiltrated the surface of Scarif. In the ensuing battle, the [[Imperial-class Star Destroyer|Star Destroyer]] ''[[Persecutor]]'' was incapacitated by rebel [[ion charge]]s and then [[Ramming|rammed]] toward the ''Intimidator'' by the Alliance [[Sphyrna-class Hammerhead corvette|''Sphyrna''-class Hammerhead corvette]] ''[[Lightmaker]]''. Although Gorin ordered his [[Star Destroyer]] to evade the ''Persecutor'', the two [[Starship|ships]] collided, and the ''Intimidator'' was sheared in two. Gorin later ceded control of his forces to [[Grand Moff]] [[Wilhuff Tarkin]] when the latter arrived on the scene aboard the [[DS-1 Orbital Battle Station|Death Star]] [[battle station]]. Following the Imperial failure at Scarif, there was contentious debate within the [[Imperial Military]] as to whether Gorin's leadership and lack of aggression or faults with the resources that he had available to him were to blame. The [[historian]] [[Beaumont Kin]] discussed these arguments and gave his own opinions on Gorin in his [[book]] ''[[The Rise and Fall of the Galactic Empire]]'' in [[35 ABY]]. ==Biography== ===An unexpected attack=== {{Quote|Sir, those are rebel ships!''"
"''Get Admiral Gorin, immediately!|An Imperial officer and Lieutenant Casido witness the Alliance Fleet's arrival|audio=Casido.flac|}} [[File:Shield_Gate-SW_Battlefront.png|thumb|left|300px|Gorin's forces protected the Shield Gate above Scarif.]] Gorin was a [[human]] [[admiral]] in the [[Imperial Navy's officer corps|officer corps]] of the [[Galactic Empire]]'s [[Imperial Navy]] during the [[Galactic Civil War]]. From aboard the [[Imperial I-class Star Destroyer|''Imperial I''-class Star Destroyer]]''[[Ultimate Star Wars, New Edition]]'' ''[[Intimidator]]'',''[[Star Wars: Geektionary: The Galaxy from A - Z]]'' he served as [[Commanding officer|commander]] of the [[Realspace|space]] above the [[planet]] [[Scarif]] in the [[Scarif system]]. Gorin acted as [[Orbital Command]] of the [[Scarif fleet]] while [[General]] [[Sotorus Ramda]] was [[Surface Command]], controlling the [[Imperial Army]]'s [[Scarif Deployment]] at the [[Citadel Tower]] on the planet below. An Imperial transmission concerning the Empire's [[Shield Gate]] above Scarif and mentioning Gorin was intercepted by the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic]] and included in the collection of documents known as ''[[The Rebel Files]]''.''[[Star Wars: The Rebel Files]]'' The Shield Gate was the sole point of access through a [[planetary shield]] to the planet's surface and was defended by the ''Intimidator'' and the ''[[Persecutor]]'', the second [[Imperial-class Star Destroyer|''Imperial''-class Star Destroyer]] under Gorin's command. In [[1 BBY]],''[[Star Wars: Timelines]]'' a [[Rogue One|rebel squad]] slipped past Gorin's forces above Scarif using a [[Mission to Eadu|stolen]] Imperial [[SW-0608|cargo shuttle]], passing through the Shield Gate and reaching the planet's surface. [[File:Rebel_Fleet_above_Scarif.jpg|thumb|right|300px|The arrival of the rebel fleet at Scarif caught Gorin by surprise.]] Aiming to steal the [[Death Star plans|plans]] to the Imperial [[DS-1 Orbital Battle Station|Death Star]] [[superweapon]] from the Citadel Tower, the rebel team [[Battle of Scarif|engaged]] Ramda's [[garrison]] while some of its members infiltrated the tower. After Imperial transmissions concerning the conflict on the surface began to be sent, part of the [[Rebel Alliance Navy|Alliance Fleet]] under the command of Admiral [[Raddus]] on board the rebel [[flagship]] ''[[Profundity]]''''[[Star Wars: The Rise and Fall of the Galactic Empire]]'' arrived above Scarif to support its [[Alliance Military|ground forces]]. Upon the arrival of the enemy [[fleet]], [[Lieutenant]] [[Casido]] ordered from the [[Bridge (starship)|bridge]] of the ''Intimidator'' for someone to inform Gorin. ===The Battle of Scarif=== {{Quote|Transmission from Admiral Gorin.''"
"''Sir, part of the rebel fleet has arrived from hyperspace and amassed outside the shield. However, the admiral believes they are no threat to the planet—|An aide and General Sotorus Ramda report to Director Orson Krennic|audio=Ramada-Gorin.flac|[[Rogue One: A Star Wars Story (novelization)|''Rogue One: A Star Wars Story'' novelization]]}} [[File:PersecutorDisabled-RO.png|thumb|left|300px|With the shield gate closed, Gold Squadron targeted the ''Persecutor''.]] As the battle above Scarif began, Gorin positioned his ships over the Shield Gate to prevent the unlikely possibility of the rebels blasting their way through the weak point it presented in the shield. He then contacted Ramda and alerted him and [[Director]] [[Orson Callan Krennic|Orson Krennic]] to the arrival of the rebel fleet but claimed that it should not pose a threat to the ground forces. On Krennic's orders, the Shield Gate above Scarif was closed, separating the rebel and Imperial fleets from their respective ground forces. Gorin's forces, including [[TIE/ln space superiority starfighter]]s deployed on his orders, then battled those of Raddus above the planet until the rebel admiral ordered the [[BTL-A4 Y-wing assault starfighter/bomber|Y-wings]] of [[Gold Squadron (Rebel Alliance)|Gold Squadron]] to launch [[ion charge]]s at the ''Persecutor'', incapacitating the vessel. Needing to take the down the Shield Gate, Raddus ordered the rebel [[Sphyrna-class Hammerhead corvette|''Sphyrna''-class Hammerhead corvette]] ''[[Lightmaker]]'' to [[Ramming|ram]] into the side of the ''Persecutor'' and push the powerless [[Star Destroyer|vessel]] off course toward the ''Intimidator''. Attempting to maneuver his [[Starship|ship]] to avoid the collision, Gorin ordered the ''Intimidator'' to reverse at full power but failed to evade the incoming Star Destroyer. Gorin watched helplessly as''[[Star Wars: Battles that Changed the Galaxy]]'' the ''Persecutor'' smashed into the ''Intimidator'', shearing the admiral's Star Destroyer in two and destroying the bridge. The ''Persecutor'' then continued on into the Shield Gate, destroying it and allowing the rebels on the planet's surface to transmit the [[Death Star]] plans to the fleet. [[File:Intimidator-PersecutorCrash.png|thumb|right|300px|Gorin's Star Destroyer was sheared in two during the Battle of Scarif.]] After the rebel fleet received the transmission, the Death Star arrived above Scarif, and Gorin ceded his authority over the engagement to the [[battle station]]'s commander, [[Grand Moff]] [[Wilhuff Tarkin]]. Ultimately, a portion of the rebels escaped with the plans after their forces sustained heavy losses, including the ''Profundity'' once the [[Dark Lord of the Sith|Sith Lord]] [[Anakin Skywalker|Darth Vader]] and [[Captain]] [[Shaef Corssin]] arrived on the Star Destroyer ''[[Devastator]]''. ===Post-battle analysis=== {{Quote|Was it just command ineptitude that explained the Imperial defeat or was there more to it? That question became a highly contentious topic within the Imperial military in the days and weeks afterward and was seized upon by the different schools of thought who argued that either Gorin had failed to use his force effectively or, more concerningly from an Imperial point of view, had never possessed the necessary forces to begin with.|Beaumont Kin, ''The Rise and Fall of the Galactic Empire''|}} [[File:Intimidator.png|thumb|left|300px|Some argued that Gorin's leadership was at fault for the loss at Scarif, while others blamed the weaponary at his disposal, including the ''Intimidator'' (pictured).]] In the [[Standard day|days]] and [[Standard week|weeks]] following Gorin's defeat at Scarif, the subject of what had caused the Imperial failure became a highly contentious topic of debate within the [[Imperial Military]]. Some argued that command ineptitude had been the cause and that Gorin had failed to use his forces in an effective manner. Others instead argued that Gorin had lacked the necessary resources to deal with the rebels, despite the Imperial forces heavily outgunning their foes. Those blaming Gorin pointed to the fact that the ''Devastator'' was able to immobilize the ''Profundity'' where Gorin had failed to and suggested Imperials utilize heavier and more concentrated firepower in the future. Those who disagreed believed that increased aggression was not a real strategy and that although the ''Intimidator'' should have been able to breach the [[Deflector shield|shields]] of the ''Profundity'', its [[weapon]]s were not adequate for combating enemy starfighters, with the rebel fighters they did destroy being the result of luck more than technical skill. [[File:GeramsTIEs-RO.png|thumb|right|300px|Beaumont Kin believed Gorin was slow to deploy TIEs at Scarif.]] In [[35 ABY]],{{RiseAndFallDate}} the [[historian]] [[Beaumont Kin]] analyzed Gorin's actions at Scarif in his''[[Star Wars: The Rise of Skywalker: The Visual Dictionary]]'' [[book]] ''[[The Rise and Fall of the Galactic Empire]]''. Kin discussed both arguments concerning Gorin's culpability in the Imperial loss and made his own observations that the admiral had failed to ever concentrate his weaponry and so allowed his attacks to be spread across the rebel fleet, also calling Gorin's deployment of [[TIE series|TIE fighters]] at the battle incredibly slow and reasoning that this was why rebel fighters had made it through the shield gate. ==Personality and traits== {{Quote|In the face of the Scarif debacle some argued—as they had done in hypothetical discussions before the battle—that Gorin had not been nearly aggressive enough in utilizing his weaponry.|Beaumont Kin, ''The Rise and Fall of the Galactic Empire''|}} When the rebel fleet first attacked above Scarif, Gorin was caught completely by surprise and incorrectly believed that they posed no threat to the Imperial forces on the planet's surface. Other Imperials later claimed that the admiral had not been nearly aggressive enough in utilizing his weaponry against the rebels. Gorin had light skin, [[Color|gray]] [[hair]], and blue [[eye]]s. ==Skills and abilities== {{Quote|Although the rebel fleet under Admiral Raddus had the benefit of surprise, and Raddus was a far better military commander than his adversary Admiral Gorin, an examination of the opposing forces suggests that the two Imperial Star Destroyers guarding the planet—the ''Intimidator'' and the ''Persecutor''—should not have been fought to a standstill and then subsequently destroyed along with the shield gate.|Beaumont Kin, ''The Rise and Fall of the Galactic Empire''|}} Beaumont Kin believed Gorin to have been a greatly inferior military commander compared to Raddus, and others in the Imperial Military also believed Corssin to have possessed greater military skill then the admiral. ==Equipment== Gorin wore a standard gray [[Imperial officer's uniform]] with three [[code cylinder]]s and a [[rank insignia plaque]] showing six blue squares during the Battle of Scarif. ==Behind the scenes== Gorin was portrayed by [[Michael Gould]] in the [[2016]] [[Star Wars Anthology Series|Anthology]] film, ''[[Rogue One: A Star Wars Story]]''. Gould filmed additional scenes as Gorin for the film that did not make the final cut. They also involved Casido's actor [[Rufus Wright]] and included lines about the ''Intimidator'' being under repair and so unable to move. They were blocked out by director [[Gareth Edwards]] before being filmed on a gimble on a sound stage set by the film's second unit.{{WebCite|url=https://www.spyhards.com/e/spymaster-interview-36-rufus-wright|text=SpyMaster Interview #36 - Rufus Wright|date=2022-12-08|format=[[Wikipedia:Podcast|Podcast]]|work=[https://www.spyhards.com spyhards.com]|archivedate=20230131094645}} ==Appearances== {{Indexpage}} *''[[Rogue One: A Star Wars Story]]'' {{1st}} *[[Rogue One: A Star Wars Story (novelization)|''Rogue One: A Star Wars Story'' novelization]] {{Ab|Rogue One: A Star Wars Story (audiobook)}} ==Sources== *''[[Star Wars: On the Front Lines]]'' *''[[Star Wars: Geektionary: The Galaxy from A - Z]]'' *''[[Star Wars: The Rebel Files]]'' *{{EncyclopediaCite|Scarif and Other Planets in the Outer Rim}} *''[[Star Wars: Battles that Changed the Galaxy]]'' *{{EncyclopediaCite|The Birth of the Rebellion}} *''[[Star Wars: The Rise and Fall of the Galactic Empire]]'' ==Notes and references== {{Reflist}} {{Interlang |cs=Gorin |de=Gorin (Admiral) |es=Gorin |fr=Gorin |ja=ゴーリン |ko=고린 |nl=Gorin |pl=Gorin |tr=Gorin }} [[Category:Humans]] [[Category:Imperial Navy admirals of the Galactic Empire]] [[Category:Individuals of unspecified gender]] [[Category:Individuals with he/him pronouns]]
